'''''Cyperus lupulinus''''', the '''Great Plains flatsedge''', is a plant species native to North America. It is widespread across southeastern [[Canada]] and the central and northeastern [[United States]] as far west as [[Wyoming]], [[Colorado]] and [[New Mexico]], with more isolated populations reported in [[Washington (state)|Washington]] ([[Asotin County]]), [[Idaho]] ([[Idaho County]]) and [[Oregon]] ([[Wallowa County, Oregon|Wallowa County]]). It grows in open, sun-lit locations such as fields, prairies, roadsides, farms, etc.<ref name=FNA>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242357683 Flora of North America, v 23 p 176. ''Cyperus lupulinus'']</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Cyperus%20lupulinus.png BONAP (Biota of North America Project) floristic synthesis, ''Cyperus lupulinus'']</ref>

==Description==
''Cyperus lupulinus''is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] herb up to {{cvt|50|cm}} tall, spreading by means of underground [[rhizome]]s. Culms are triangular in cross-section. Spikes are densely clustered into a more or less spherical clump. [[Achene]]s are dark brown, almost black, egg-shaped, about {{cvt|2|mm|frac=64}} across.<ref name=FNA/><ref>Marcks, Brian. 1974. Transactions of the Wisconsin Academy of Sciences, Arts and Letters 62: 271.</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/ImageFullView.aspx?imageid=100203480 photo of a herbarium specimen of ''Cyperus lupulinus'' at Missouri Botanical Garden, collected in Missouri 1994.]</ref><ref>Sprengel, Curt Polycarp Joachim. 1807. Mantissa Prima Florae Halensis 1: 30.</ref><ref>Great Plains Flora Association. 1986. Flora of the Great Plains i–vii, 1–1392. University Press of Kansas, Lawrence.</ref><ref>Wunderlin, R. P. 1998. Guide to the Vascular Plants of Florida i–x, 1–806. University Press of Florida, Gainesville.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
Two [[subspecies]] are accepted:<ref name=theplantlist/><ref name=FNA/>

*''Cyperus lupulinus'' subsp. ''lupulinus'' - Floral scales greater than 2.5 mm, not clasping achenes; [[spikelet]]s with 5-22 scales each
*''Cyperus lupulinus'' subsp. ''macilentus'' <small>(Fernald) Marcks</small> - Floral scales less than 2.5 mm, clasping achenes; spikelets with 3-7 scales each
